rows.answer:
When a customer exceeds their limit, the API returns **HTTP 429**. The response includes a `Retry-After` header giving the number of seconds to wait [1]. Customers don't have to guess when to retry: the header tells them exactly how long to wait.

- **Response:** HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header in seconds [1].
- **Retry timing:** Our SDKs honor `Retry-After` automatically and back off exponentially [1]. Customers using the HTTP API directly would need to read that header and wait themselves. The sources don't describe retry behavior for raw HTTP clients beyond the header.
- **Quota impact:** Rejected requests don't count against the monthly event quota [1].
- **Scope:** Limits apply per workspace, not per API key, so multiple keys in one workspace share one budget [1].
- **Bursts:** Short bursts up to 2x the limit are allowed for 10 seconds [1].
- **Not a 429:** If an endpoint isn't included in a customer's plan, it returns HTTP 403, not 429 [1].

If a customer needs higher limits, Enterprise ingest limits on `/v2/events` and `/v2/events/batch` can be raised up to 3x the default by contract, through the account team and the Data Plane queue. Growth plan limits are fixed by contract, and temporary raises for a one-off backfill (up to 72 hours) can be granted by the Data Plane on-call primary [1].

| Incident | Severity | Service | Owning team |
|---|---|---|---|
| INC-2278 (Jul 28) | SEV-2 | Driftwood | PLAT [2][6] |
| INC-2291 (Aug 14) | SEV-1 | ingest-gateway | DP [2][6] |
| INC-2302 (Aug 27) | SEV-2 | Keystone | IDB [2][6] |
| INC-2327 (Sep 29) | SEV-2 | Beacon | OBS [2][6] |
| INC-2340 (Oct 6) | SEV-2 | Ledger | IDB [2][6] |

Team codes expand as follows: DP is Data Plane, PLAT is Platform, IDB is Identity & Billing, and OBS is Observability [11].

So Data Plane owned two of the incidents (INC-2291 and INC-2351), Identity & Billing owned two (INC-2302 and INC-2340), and Platform and Observability each owned one.

The incident log does not track owning teams itself; I mapped each service to its owner using the service catalog [2][6]. **Keep trying for 30 minutes. If you still can't reach the ordering clinician, the result goes to the on-call medical director.** The protocol requires critical results to reach the ordering clinician within 60 minutes, and the 30-minute mark is when you escalate [1].

To reach the on-call medical director, call the Halcyon answering service at 555-0144 and choose option 2. The service pages the on-call director and pages the backup if there's no callback within 10 minutes. Don't text physicians' personal mobile numbers [3].

Document every critical result notification in the chart, with the time and the person notified [1].

The November rota doesn't name the on-call director for Wednesday, November 18, so confirm who is on duty when you call [3].

The knowledge base doesn't list a self-pay price for an RSV vaccine. Halcyon's 2026–27 in-clinic vaccine formulary, which lists all self-pay vaccine prices, has no RSV entry [1].

The formulary does include the recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV), which is for shingles, not RSV. It's $205 per dose for patients aged 50 and over, with a second dose 2–6 months later [1]. Other self-pay vaccine prices in the formulary include:

- Influenza, standard-dose: $35 (ages 6 months to 64) [1]
- Influenza, high-dose: $72 (ages 65 and over) [1]
- COVID-19 (2026–27 formula): $140 (ages 12 and over) [1]
- PCV20 pneumococcal: $265 [1]

The 20% prompt-pay discount doesn't apply to vaccine prices, though sliding-fee program patients do get that program's discount [1]. If you need an RSV price, check with the clinical pharmacist or the billing team, since it isn't in the current documents.

Halcyon doesn't use the "buddy" term, but it has a close equivalent: every new clinical hire is paired with a **preceptor for 90 days** [1]. The preceptor is your main point of contact during that period. You'll have weekly check-ins for the first month, then check-ins every other week [1]. Your preceptor also signs off on your competency checklist at 30, 60 and 90 days [1].

For comparison, Northwind's new-hire guide says your manager and onboarding buddy will walk you through your first two weeks [2]. It doesn't give a buddy duration in the sources I found.

rows.answer:
**Northwind Labs (October invoices):** The fix makes invoice creation idempotent per workspace and billing period, so a second run can't create a second invoice for the same period [2][3]. The root cause was that the payment provider's webhook timed out, the retry logic re-ran the batch, and invoice creation wasn't idempotent [3]. The fix was merged and deployed the same day, and a dry run of the job showed zero duplicates [3]. The changelog lists this as an internal item [2]. The INC-2340 postmortem was due October 13, but I didn't find it in the results, so I can't confirm any further action items [3][4].

**Halcyon Health (September reminders):** There are three changes [1]:
- Each reminder now carries an idempotency key made from the patient, medication, and scheduled time. A reminder with an existing key is never sent again [1].
- Scheduler cutovers now require a written runbook and clinical safety sign-off [1]. The clinical change policy says a runbook for a cutover must state how double-running is prevented, and the rule came from this incident [5].
- Reminder messages now tell patients, "If you already took this dose, you don't need to take it again" [1].

The duplicates happened because a September 2 configuration change moved the reminder scheduler to a new job runner, and both the old and new runners were active during the cutover [1].

sources.title: Incident review: duplicate medication reminders (IR-0412)
sources.snippet: A configuration change on September 2 moved the reminder scheduler to a new job runner. During the cutover, both the old and the new runners were active. Neither checked whether a reminder had already been sent, because the old system relied on being the only sender.

rows.answer:
**Halcyon offers the bigger discount, at 20% versus Northwind's 15%.** The two aren't directly comparable, though, because they apply to different products.

- **Northwind:** Annual prepayment on the Growth plan earns a 15% discount, which works out to $12,240 per year [1]. The June-era discount rules were replaced in October, but the 15% prepayment discount was explicitly kept [5].
- **Halcyon:** Self-pay patients who pay in full at the time of service get a 20% prompt-pay discount [3]. This doesn't apply to vaccines and injectables, which are already priced at cost plus administration [2]. Patients in the sliding-fee program get that program's discount instead [2][3].
